redFlags.source: Wikipedia, 1984 Monaco Grand Prix: 'The red flag to stop the race was shown at the end of the 32nd lap', positions counted 'from the last lap completed by every driver' (lap 31; citing Autocourse 1984-85 p.141), scheduled 76 laps, 31 laps classified (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Monaco_Grand_Prix); C. Bradley, 'When Senna and Bellof starred in Monaco, as Prost prevailed', Autosport (edited 3 Jun 2023): 'red-flagged halfway through lap 32', 'the race result was backdated to lap 31' (https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/when-senna-and-bellof-starred-in-monaco-as-prost-prevailed/6530051/)
redFlags.note: Not resumed; half points (Prost 4.5). Sources differ on when in lap 32 the flag came: Wikipedia 'at the end of the 32nd lap', Autosport 'halfway through lap 32'; both put it on lap 32. The Wikipedia list's 'lap 31' is the classification lap, not the flag lap.
